# Timestamp writer-convention classification — 2026-09-23

**FID:** FID-20260923-001 (step 1: classify before migrating) · **Mode:** evidence-only, no DB writes
**Generated by:** `npx tsx scripts/classifyTimestampColumns.ts`
**Process TZ:** `America/New_York` (offset at probe: -4.00h) · **DB session TZ:** `UTC` · **DB UTC wall at probe:** `2026-09-23 17:40:21`

## Method

1. **Provenance (static)** — `information_schema.column_default` plus every write site in the runtime
   corpus. Attribution is **ownership by nearest write statement**: every `.insert(<ident>)`/
   `.update(<ident>)` / raw `INSERT INTO` / `UPDATE` line is an anchor for its table, and an assignment
   `prop: value` is attributed to the anchor within **40 lines**, only when that anchor names the
   column's table. Both write shapes are covered — inline (`values({ createdAt: new Date() })`, Δ0) and
   deferred (`const row = { createdAt: new Date() }; … values(row)`). Every site in §Write sites
   reports its Δ so the attribution can be audited.

   *A stricter parser was tried and rejected.* A hand-rolled TS statement splitter (bracket/quote
   aware, splitting on `;`) **desynchronised on regex and template literals**, producing one region
   spanning hundreds of lines that misattributed `mapDomainPlayerToRow` to an insert and **missed the
   decisive `lib/playerService.ts:410`**. It was caught by re-reading the report, not by the tool, and is
   recorded here so it is not reintroduced.
2. **Population (live)** — row count, non-null count, min/max, zero-time-of-day count, future count,
   and the `now() - value` histogram.
3. **Clustering (live)** — for every sibling anchor that is a true instant (`timestamptz`, or a naive
   column the DB itself stamps with `DEFAULT now()`), the per-row delta `anchor_utc_wall - value` is
   clustered at 15-minute granularity. Two tight clusters separated by the process offset (4h/5h)
   **prove** two writing conventions in one column.

**Calibration (read-only, no table touched).** A known instant passed as a JS `Date` through this driver:

| representation | value | reading |
| --- | --- | --- |
| true instant | `2026-01-15T12:00:00.000Z` | UTC |
| what the wire carries | `2026-01-15T07:00:00.000-05:00` | ISO with offset — unambiguous |
| into a `timestamptz` | `2026-01-15 12:00:00` | **correct** — the instant survives |
| into a `timestamp` (naive) | `2026-01-15 07:00:00` | **process-local wall clock** — the offset is dropped |

So a naive column written by the app stores the process-local wall clock, while a naive column written by
`DEFAULT now()` (DB session = UTC) stores the UTC wall clock: the two differ by exactly the process offset.

**Coverage and the `now()` anchor.** `now() - value` only discriminates when something wrote within the
offset (4h). On this database the youngest value anywhere is `factories.last_attack_time`
at **21.41h old**, and there are 0 rows with any value inside the 8h window — the now-anchor
cannot fire. The sibling anchors carry the live leg: **10 pair-tests over 8 of 135 columns** (only
tables holding a `timestamptz` column or a `DEFAULT now()` naive column can be anchored at all).

## Live-layer coverage (honest limits)

The sibling-anchor test ran **10 pair-tests over 8 of 135 columns**. An anchor needs a
`timestamptz` sibling (a true instant) or a `DEFAULT now()` naive sibling (a UTC wall clock) in the **same table**:

| anchored column | anchor | rows | clusters |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `flag_trail.expires_at` | `flag_trail.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 3 | -0.25h×3 |
| `players.created_at` | `players.protection_until` (timestamptz) | 42 | 72.00h×42 |
| `players.last_level_up` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 1 | -196.25h×1 |
| `players.last_login_date` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 1 | -229.00h×1 |
| `players.last_streak_reward` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 1 | -229.00h×1 |
| `players.last_xp_award` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 13 | -49.75h×2, -289.75h×1, -287.75h×1 |
| `players.vip_expiration` | `players.protection_until` (timestamptz) | 1 | -648.00h×1 |
| `players.vip_expiration` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 2 | -8835.50h×1, -720.00h×1 |
| `players.vip_last_updated` | `players.protection_until` (timestamptz) | 1 | 72.00h×1 |
| `players.vip_last_updated` | `players.created_at` (db-default-naive) | 1 | 0.00h×1 |

Everything else is **static-only**: its convention rests on provenance, not on a live measurement.
Two ways to close that gap, neither taken here because both write: (1) re-run during an active game session,
when the `now()` anchor fires; (2) a `BEGIN; INSERT …; measure; ROLLBACK` probe per table, which still needs a
NOT-NULL map per table.
